levels.label: Small
levels.description: A small, contained change in one area of the code, touching about 5 files or fewer: a bug fix, a typo, copy, style, config or docs edit, or a small addition to an existing feature. No new data model, state design or public API.

levels.label: Medium
levels.description: A feature or fix across one or two areas, roughly 5 to 15 files, that adds or changes behaviour worth its own tests and a code review. It is still one coherent change: it does not split into parallel parts and needs no new design for state, data model, concurrency or persistence.

levels.label: Large
levels.description: Complex and broad work where at least two of these hold: 3 or more issues, or changes across several packages or areas that can run as parallel lanes; a new design for state, data model, concurrency or persistence; roughly 15 or more files or 500 or more changed lines. One area or a long task alone is not enough.

level.question: This is a coding task for an AI coding agent. Which level of process does it need? Judge the scope of the change it asks for: how many areas and files it touches, whether it needs a new design, and whether it splits into parallel parts.

recipe.question: This is a coding task for an AI coding agent. Which saved recipe covers it? A recipe covers the task only when the task is the kind of work the recipe's title describes.
recipe.none: No saved recipe covers this task.

ui.question: These are the changed files and the commit subjects of a finished coding task. Did the task change anything a user sees or interacts with in an app's user interface?
ui.yes: Yes: it changes screens, pages, components, styles, layout, visible text or interaction in an app's user interface.
ui.no: No: it changes only back-end code, data, tooling, scripts, tests, docs or configuration, with nothing visible in an app's user interface.
